author: Inside Edition
description: More of Jane Doe's secretly recorded phone conversations with the fraternity brothers she says gang raped her have been revealed. The unidentified woman told Cornell University student Winston Lee she was reaching out, trying to piece everything together. Lee appeared suspicious of the call. Shortly after the call, the university held disciplinary hearings for the seven students Jane Doe says attacked her. Lee was suspended for two years, but is back on campus completing his senior year. Jane Doe has sued Cornell University and the seven fraternity brothers. They have not been criminally charged and deny wrongdoing.
title: Was There A Coverup By The Cornell Frat Brothers?

author: Inside Edition
description: There are more eyebrow-raising bombshells from Hollywood legend Michael Douglas' new memoir, "One Helluva Ride." The book's title is an apt description of the actor's love life. He's been married to Catherine Zeta-Jones for a quarter of a century, but as a bachelor, Douglas played the field. The 82-year-old Oscar winner shoots down reports he was treated for sex addiction, and wants to set the record straight.
title: Michael Douglas' Love Life Was 'One Helluva Ride'

author: Inside Edition
description: Alleghia Botner is the ex-mistress at the center of the former "American Idol" contestant's murder trial. Botner found herself being denounced at Monday's sentencing by the two daughters of Caleb Flynn, who was convicted of murdering his wife so he could start a new life with his mistress. Now, Botner's lawyer is reacting to the shocking letters read in court.
title: Ex-Mistress' Lawyer Reacts To Statements From Caleb Flynn's Daughters

author: Inside Edition
description: President Trump appeared at a raucous rally in Nebraska, and by his side was seemingly ever-present presidential aide Natalie Harp. Harp got quite a compliment from her boss, including a reference to "The Price Is Right." When Harp brought out an executive order about diesel fuel for Trump to sign, the commander-in-chief called her "perfect." Harp is not the only presidential staffer being thrust into the spotlight. Last week at a rally in Oklahoma, it was long-time assistant Margo Martin.
title: Trump Evokes 'Price Is Right' To Praise Natalie Harp At Nebraska Rally

author: Inside Edition
description: It's being called a real-life "Parent Trap," and it all happened at a softball game. Two girls playing on opposing teams found out they shared much more than just a passing resemblance to each other. Samantha Rensvold and Kyann Dean were playing a Montana high school softball tournament when someone noticed they looked like mirror images of each other. There was a simple explanation for that: the two were sisters who had been adopted by different families.
title: High School Softball Players On Opposing Teams Realize They're Sisters

author: Inside Edition
description: The next inmate set to be executed in Tennessee is getting a temporary reprieve, after the failed execution of Christa Pike. Gary Wayne Sutton was set to be executed on December 3rd. Governor Bill Lee halted all executions in the state, pending the outcome of an investigation into what went wrong with the most recent attempt at administering lethal injection. According to her attorney, Christa Pike remains in critical condition. Inside Edition Digital’s Mara Montalbano has more.
title: Tennessee's Next Lethal Injection Halted After Failed Execution Of Christa Pike

author: Inside Edition
description: Did an Idaho investigator, looking into a local cold case, solve a 40-year-old mystery in Illinois? The production team at "Unsolved Mysteries" believes two cases may have been solved in one investigation: that a man, found dead in a Boise church in 1982, was the person who killed seven people with cyanide in Tylenol bottles around the Chicago area earlier that year. An upcoming documentary will make a case for this new suspect. Inside Edition Digital’s Mara Montalbano has more.
title: Was This Man The Tylenol Killer?

author: Inside Edition
description: Italian authorities say 377 exotic animals were intercepted before they could be trafficked to another country. The Guardia di Finanza, the country's financial law enforcement agency, says the animals were discovered in a car at a port in Sicily bound for Malta. Officials say the driver of the car was a Maltese citizen found in possession of 300 tortoises and 77 parrots. Most of them were protected species. Inside Edition Digital’s Mara Montalbano has more.
title: 377 Exotic Animals Seized At Port In Sicily
